flashcards.back: A number between 0 and 1 that measures how likely an event is: 0 means impossible and 1 means certain.
One possible result of a trial, such as heads on a single coin toss.
A set of outcomes we are interested in, such as throwing exactly one head in two tosses.
Outcomes that share the same probability, like the four cells of the two-toss table at 1/4 each.
The set of all possible outcomes of a trial - for two coin tosses it has four members.
Events where the result of one does not change the probabilities of the other, so their probabilities multiply.

A streak feels like it must balance out. The coin has no memory: the next toss is still 1/2. In class, toss a coin until three heads land in a row, then ask the class to bet on the next toss: whatever the streak, the fresh toss is still 1/2 heads and 1/2 tails.
